130121.overview:
Fire is a Game & Watch game released as a part of the Silver series on July 31, 1980, and as a part of the Wide Screen series on December 4, 1981. It is a single-screen single-player Game & Watch.

The player controls two firemen who carry a trampoline and must catch people who fall from a burning building and bounce them into a waiting ambulance. The player is awarded 3 points for each person who reaches the ambulance, and loses one of their three lives for each person who hits the ground.

135117.overview: Players have to press buttons that correspond with the number shown to make the pirate either hold a flag or show his feet. The better the player gets at the game, the harder the game gets. If the player presses the wrong button at any time, that player will lose a life.

149339.overview: This game was released outside Japan as Fishing Boy.

162006.overview: Fire Attack involves a cowboy who is using a hammer to try to stop attackers (represented as stereotypical Native Americans) from burning down his base. Every time the player hits a torch or an attacker, they receive two points. As the game progresses, the player will have to be a lot more cautious as more attackers appear. If an attacker manages to set the base on fire, the player will get a miss. If the player reaches 200 or 500 points without any misses, every torch or attacker the player hits will be worth five points for 30 to 50 seconds. If the player has any misses at either score, all misses will be removed instead. When the player gets three misses, they receive a Game Over. In Game A, attackers come from three directions, but they change positions and come from different directions after a miss is made. In Game B, attackers come from four directions, and the game gets faster sooner.

190484.overview:
Frogger follows the perilous journey of a frog determined to return home. The frog must cross a busy highway and a river filled with moving logs and creatures, dodging danger at every step. The premise mirrors the original Konami arcade game released the same year, condensed for Coleco’s miniature tabletop format.

Players control the frog using a four-direction joystick positioned on the front panel. The goal is to move the frog upward through two distinct zones: a lower section representing a multi-lane road and an upper section symbolizing a river. Vehicles in the roadway flash across the display, and contact with them costs the player a life. In the river zone, the frog must hop between moving logs and avoid sinking into the water. Successful navigation into one of the home bays at the top of the screen advances the stage and increases difficulty.

The VFD display renders all motion in bright green and red segments, accompanied by simple sound effects for hopping, collisions, and successful arrivals. The gameplay loop remains faithful to the arcade’s structure but simplified for hardware limitations—fewer lanes, fewer simultaneous enemies, and a slower pace suitable for the small tabletop device.

200757.overview: Football 2 is a sequel to Football. It builds upon the gameplay established by the first game with some additional options such as running backwards and passing. Aside from the two difficulties that the original game also had it's also possible to go to hidden third and fourth difficulties by holding the pass button while selecting the difficulty. The original version uses an LED display, the later re-release uses an LCD display.

422780.overview:
Gunfighter by Bandai (released on December 30, 1980) is a classic, highly collectible handheld electronic game that recreates a Wild West duel. In Japan, it was famously released under the name FL Gun Professional (or Duel).

 Two players sit side-by-side. Using directional buttons, you move your cowboy up and down to dodge shots while hitting the fire button to eliminate your opponent. You can also strategically shoot through the cactuses to clear a line of sight.

477854.overview:
Fred Flintstone always comes up with a great idea - and this time he wants you to score points by helping him pick up as many rocks as he can before time runs out! Of course he has his trusty "Shovel-Saurus" to help him do the job, but he also has some obstacles to avoid. Barney is a great friend but when he tries to help Fred, he becomes Fred's biggest obstacle! Help Fred avoid Barney and other pending disasters, before the boss, Mr. Slate, pays Fred a visit! A successful rock haul will bring Wilma, Betty and Dino out to greet you!

At the Slate Rock and Gravel Company, time is money - so pick up as many rocks as you can!

Help Fred finish his work before Mr. Slate comes out to yell at him - or you'll lose precious time!

Watch out! Barney will try and help, but he's making it harder for Fred! Don't crash into his Shovel-Saurus!
